Discuss in a short academic paragraph how preserving an obsolete train timetable can help historians study everyday mobility; mention one limitation of that source without inventing citations. Aim for approximately 120–170 English tokens.

message.content: Preserved railway timetables, though obsolete for travelers, offer historians a structured record of everyday mobility. They reveal which towns were connected, how frequently services ran, and at what hours, allowing scholars to infer patterns of commuting, market travel, and leisure excursions. Comparing successive editions can show how changing schedules reflected shifts in industry, settlement, and working routines, while the distinction between express and local services hints at social and economic hierarchies of access. Timetables also illuminate the temporal texture of daily life, since standardized departure times shaped expectations about punctuality and the organization of work and school. However, these documents record intended rather than actual service. Delays, cancellations, overcrowding, and unofficial adjustments rarely appear, so historians must supplement timetables with diaries, newspapers, or operational records to understand how journeys were truly experienced and who was able to make them.
